reference_answer: AbbVie describes a series of governance and legal provisions that are designed to deter hostile takeovers and coercive bids. The company uses a staggered board structure, with directors divided into three classes serving staggered three-year terms, which is a well-known structural defense that makes it difficult for an acquirer to gain full board control in a single election. In addition, directors can only be removed for cause, which serves as a board entrenchment defense. While this is not a contractual arrangement like a golden parachute, it has a comparable effect in that it makes it significantly harder to displace existing leadership during a takeover attempt. AbbVie further entrenches board control by stipulating that only directors, and not stockholders, may fill vacancies. Shareholder influence is also restricted by the inability of stockholders to call special meetings, limiting the capacity of investors to initiate governance changes in the context of a hostile bid. Another layer of defense is a supermajority voting requirement, which mandates that at least 80 percent of AbbVie’s voting stock must approve amendments to certain governance provisions, creating a high threshold for potential acquirors who might otherwise seek to alter board structure or shareholder rights. Finally, AbbVie is protected by Section 203 of the Delaware General Corporation Law, which restricts any shareholder acquiring more than 15 percent of the company’s stock from engaging in business combinations with AbbVie for three years, effectively preventing a rapid follow-on merger or “toe-hold” strategy. According to AbbVie, these measures are intended to safeguard stockholders from coercive or unfair takeover tactics by ensuring negotiations with the board and allowing more time to evaluate offers. At the same time, the company acknowledges that these provisions could delay or prevent transactions that some shareholders might view as beneficial and may also make it more difficult to remove incumbent directors.

Taken together, these moves show AbbVie’s intent to secure leadership stability while investing in high-growth, innovative therapies, positioning the company for sustainable success beyond its current product base.
